messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — GeoDNS health alert: increased 502/504s observed from EU-edge (eu-west-1) over last 3m. Route53 answer set shows mixed records; TTLs are inconsistent across edge resolvers. Paging eu-cloud-oncall.

mike.j: seeing this too — dig from 3 different EU resolvers returns: one returns old CNAME -> legacy-lb.redwood.internal, others return new active-lb. TTL on old record is 86400. Noticed spike at 14:02 UTC.

tanvi: Cloudflare resolver metrics show a surge in NODATA and SERVFAIL around same time, but then some resolvers started returning the old record. Could be stale cache propagation on CF resolvers.

susan: Customer reports: multiple EU customers routing to retired backend causing 5xxs. Impacted ~12% of EU traffic. Confirmed error rate ~48% for eu requests to /v1/generate.

alex: quick check — Route53 change history shows we rolled a CNAME update at 13:50 UTC (change id ZRXXXX). The change completed but TTL 24h on previous record could cause caching at upstream resolvers. We probably didn't invalidate caches.

mike.j: mitigation options: 1) force Route53 to re-wind by creating a new record with short TTL and swap weights (risky) 2) update health checks and failover config to route traffic away from legacy LB 3) ask CF to purge (only affects CF resolvers).

susan: we need fast customer impact reduction. I can start a GeoDNS weight shift to send traffic to us-west as fallback (lower latency hit but avoids retired backend). Will that be immediate?

alex: weight changes take effect in Route53 quickly, but resolvers honoring cache TTL may still return old answer until their TTL expires. However, many resolvers do pick up new answers quickly on subsequent queries. Go for weight shift + reduce TTL on new record.

mike.j: I can cut the TTL on the new active record to 60s via a change batch. Preparing change batch now:

```
# aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"CNAME","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"active-lb.redwood.internal"}]}}]}'
```

tanvi: I'll open a CF support ticket requesting a resolver-side purge for the stale CNAME answers in EU edge POPs. Adding logs and sample dig outputs.

support-bot: Note added to ticket TRACK-5281 with summary "CF resolver stale cache for api.redwood.example — affecting eu-west-1".

susan: weight shift started: increasing us-west pool to 90% for eu traffic via GeoDNS policy. Monitoring now.

mike.j: TTL change applied at 14:10 UTC. Change id ZRYYYY. Route53 reports INSYNC.

alex: monitoring traces — backend 5xxs are dropping. at 14:14 UTC error rate down to ~18% in EU. Still seeing noisy spikes from a subset of resolvers.

tanvi: CF support replied: they queued a purge and are forcing revalidation on EU POPs; ETA ~10-12m. They asked for sample dig outputs which I posted.

susan: customer comms: drafting status — short note explaining partial degradation, mitigation in progress, no data loss, workaround in place (routing to fallback region). Will post to status page once we have stable metrics <5% errors for 5m.

mike.j: next steps: keep TTL at 60s for 1 hour, after stabilization plan to increase TTL back to recommended value and roll a controlled migration of remaining traffic. File follow-up action to review change process that left a long TTL on a transitional cname.

alex: oncall handoff — I'm taking next shift at 15:00 UTC. Leaving doc in incident board with current state. Please escalate to SRE lead if error rate >25% after 15:20 UTC.

oncall-bot: Handoff: alex is now the primary oncall for this thread.

support-bot: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai incident/INC-2026: "Partial routing disruption in EU — mitigation in progress. See updates."

susan: final note before handoff — CF purge appears to have landed, residual resolver cache TTLs expiring. EU error rate steady at 3.2% for last 6m. Marking incident as mitigated; will keep under observation.

alex: thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups: ACTION-113: postmortem (owner: susan), ACTION-114: add pre-change TTL check to rollout playbook (owner: mike.j), ACTION-115: add automated GeoDNS weight rollback trigger by error-rate (owner: tanvi). Closing live incident thread and moving to postmortem channel.
